_artwork/skills/gallery.title: gallery
_artwork/skills/gallery.content:
Skills illustrations
Current illustrated pages; the original PNGs and prompts retain their generation history. All manual plates.
Atlatl Throwing
Skills page
Three small separated outline side-profile figures show SAME ordinary human in three positions, with NO overlapping ghostlimbs: balanced setup, coordinated forward movement, follow-through. Each has exactly two arms/two legs; modest natural clothing. Slender wooden atlatl with small supported spur engaging rear seat of long BLUNT UNFLETCHED dart at setup; appropriate overarm throw with body turn, later lever rises, projectile clears hook. No giant crook, fletching, bow or spearhead. Labels ‘BALANCE’, ‘COORDINATE’, ‘FOLLOW THROUGH’. Conceptual motion plate not mastered narrative action. Dashed path only beyond release.

Basic Foraging
Skills page
Close still-life technique study of a whole hazel twig with rounded toothed leaves, intact husked hazelnuts and opened nut showing cream kernel, plus hands sorting sound nuts from cracked dark moulding rejected one into separate bark scraps. Label ‘IDENTIFY WHOLE PLANT’, ‘EDIBLE PORTION’, ‘COUNT PROCESSING’. Positive identified hazel teachingexample, not generic edible wild plant key. No tasting unknown leaves, mushrooms, rich harvest heap or modern measuring scale.

Basic Spear Fishing
Skills page
Single educational water-refraction cross-section, no catching scene. Person simplified only at bank with bare feet on STABLE DRY GROUND, wooden-pointed spear tip near surface, water shallow and slow. Real fish clearly drawn below surface; dotted pale duplicate ABOVE real fish labelled ‘APPARENT POSITION’. Light ray bends at surface consistently; aim ray points below apparent image toward realfish. Labels ‘STABLE FOOTING’, ‘REFRACTION’, ‘REAL POSITION’. No impaled fish, deep wading or boat.

Basic Thatching
Skills page
Close side-section of sloped small timber shelter framework. Hands placing an upper grass bundle course over the top of lower course; clearly downhill direction with a few blue water arrows on TOP of outer thatch leading down off eave, never into roof. Two courses overlapping like shingles. Label ‘WORK UPWARD’, ‘OVERLAPPING COURSES’, ‘KEEP OPENINGS CLEAR’. No indoor hearth or metal roof.

Berry Foraging
Skills page
One botanical bramble twig bearing recognisable clustered blackberries with toothed compound leaves and thorns. Hand selecting one sound ripe black berry, small clean bark tray below, separate squashed sample isolated. Labels ‘CONFIRM THE PLANT’, ‘SOUND FRUIT’, ‘SMALL CLEAN LOT’. No generic redberry edibility code or invented exact specieskey, plentiful basket, cooking apparatus.

Bifacial Knapping
Skills page
A blank and opposite faces of a rough biface, emphasising work on both faces.

Bow Drill Fire
Skills page
Side three-quarter close technique study: dry flat hearth board socket near edge with V-notch joining socket to outside edge and small bark ember catcher UNDER notch. Vertical spindle held at top by bearing block in operator hand; other hand holds curved wooden bow, single cord wraps spindle once. Foot braces board away from notch; bearing wrist supported against shin, bow path unobstructed. No flame; tiny dark dust mound at notch. Inset sustained small ember separate from smoke icon. Labels ‘STABLE BEARING’, ‘DUST NOTCH’, ‘EMBER CATCHER’. Show at most cropped lower body, two hands, one foot.

Communication and Exchange
Skills page
Two clothed schematic human adults several paces apart, one open palm held low and the other calm raised stop palm, both normal upright anatomy. A small neutral wooden sample lies beside first adult, NOT passed hand to hand. Broken arc on ground conveys distance; open retreat arrow away from encounter. Labels ‘OBSERVE DISTANCE’, ‘RESPECT REFUSAL’, ‘SHARED MEANING’. No speech transcript, hand shaking, barter piles or celebration. Universal reference skill, not invented trading in current story.

Crayfish Gathering
Skills page
Conceptual assessment plate, NOT a local occurrence claim: isolated generic freshwater crayfish in natural ochre/blue labelled ‘CONFIRM SPECIES’. Secondary shallow-water bank section, hand kept ABOVE rock rather than reaching blindly beneath it; footprint on dry stablebank. Small closed empty bark specimen tray. Labels ‘CHECK LOCAL PRESENCE’, ‘STABLE FOOTING’, ‘DO NOT REACH BLINDLY’. No catch, meal, eating, red boiled shell or predicted yield.

Edible Plant Identification
Skills page
Assessment plate with one whole neutral botanical specimen drawn roots/stem/leaves/fruit together and three enlarged feature callouts: leaf attachment, flower structure, fruit. None labelled as edible species, no taste action. Add simple paired outlines of similar plants with one discriminating feature highlighted. Labels ‘WHOLE ORGANISM’, ‘COMPARE FEATURES’, ‘CHECK LOOKALIKES’. No universal toxicity code, identified edible mushroom, taste test or one-feature safety rule.

Environmental Observation
Skills page
Hand-drawn conceptual terrain study with small shelter icon on drained highground, stream line downhill, open escape arrow and tiny footprint/smoke sign marked question near ridge. NOT literal surveyed valley map: use no compass scale or numbered travel distances. Insets a hand checking soil dampness and three simple repeated observations. Labels ‘OBSERVE’, ‘COMPARE’, ‘REVISIT’. No certainty about owners or motives, second suppliedcamp.

Flint Knapping Basics
Skills page
Close hands on well-supported knappablecore with a small roundedhammerstone poised above exposed edge; intended removal path away from handandleg. Two isolated flakes and a small hinged removal comparison. Navy leaderlines labels ‘SOUND PLATFORM’, ‘CONTROLLED STRIKE’, ‘INSPECT REMOVAL’. No metalchisels, huge perfect handaxe, pressureflakingantler, exactuniversalangle or cutskin. Fingers kept behind workingedge.

Hand Drill Fire
Skills page
Conceptual alternative: slender straight dry wooden spindle vertical in a notched hearth board on ground; two open palms facing each other on opposite sides of spindle, arrows showing rotation and downward pressure. Cropped knee helps brace board; small catcher beneath notch. No bow, cord or bearing block. No flame or guaranteed ember. Labels ‘ROTATE’, ‘CONTROL PRESSURE’, ‘EMBER NOT SMOKE’. Generic prepared wood, no identifiable poisonous stems.

Hunting Approach
Skills page
A field-manual study of observation, screened approach and a clear return route.

Knots - Primitive Set
Skills page
An accurately traced natural two-strand cord with ONE simple overhand stopper knot enlarged as main study: rope doubles into loop, free end passes once through the loop and is drawn into a single overhand knot. Small inset shows generous free tail under low test tension and witness mark for slipping. NOT a bowline, snare, decorative tangle or detached rope ring. Labels ‘DRESS THE KNOT’, ‘LEAVE A TAIL’, ‘CHECK FOR CREEP’. Only ONE knot illustrated; page lists other knots in prose.

Measurement and Records
Skills page
Hands compare one plain notched wooden reference rod to a second short workpiece, starting ends aligned on bark mat. Separate small bark slip shows two groups of simple unconnected tally strokes. Spare small similar kernellots not largefoodheap. Labels ‘SAME REFERENCE’, ‘ALIGN THE ENDS’, ‘RECORD FAILURES’. No Arabic numerals, SIcalibration, metal ruler, modernnotebook, balanceorcommunalstandards.

Medicinal Plant Assessment
Skills page
Quiet research-assessment plate: neutral botanical sprig, small unfilled bark tray and bark record slip with unnumbered simple marks. Three separated leader areas ‘IDENTITY’, ‘PREPARATION’, ‘EVIDENCE’. Small hand holds sprig for inspection, no mortarful remedy, infusion dose, wound, treatment or sterile claim. Distinguish consideration from application; no medical symbols promising cure.

Mushroom Foraging
Skills page
Reference identification framework: two isolated non-labelled generic mushrooms, one shown complete with cap, stem, gills, intact base and substrate; small enlarged detail of underside and base. Emphasise observation and uncertainty with labels ‘WHOLE SPECIMEN’, ‘CHECK THE BASE’, ‘LEAVE UNCERTAIN’. No green edible checkmark, safety diagnosis, tasting, harvested mushroom basket or safe-versus-poison speciespair. No meal.

Mussel Harvesting
Skills page
Two closed generic freshwater bivalve research specimens in isolation, with a partly exposed one on shallow sediment inset; observer’s foot on stable dry bank, no barefoot sweeping. Short labels ‘IDENTIFY SPECIES’, ‘ASSESS WATER SOURCE’, ‘KEEP SEPARATE’. Small clean empty bark research tray, not cooked mussels or meal. No universal edible checkmarks or assertion heating removes toxins.

Projectile Testing
Skills page
Top-down small generic experimental ground, NOT surveyed valleymap. Clear short start position faces broad EARTH BANK backstop, tiny dispersed dart landing marks with two separate trial groups in dusty blue/coral. A slim blunt unfletched dart and separate small thrower lie isolated at edge. One bark tally slip has simple strokes. Labels ‘SAME START’, ‘RECORD MISSES’, ‘CHANGE ONE FACTOR’. No speed/energy/range numbers, bullseye victory, people in path or pointed huntingdart.

Retreat Planning
Skills page
Conceptual route-and-load plate: small primary shelter icon and an EMPTY natural rock-screened bench, dotted alternative walking route stays on SAME SIDE of stream without crossing deep water. Modest essentials isolated: wooden-pointed spear, stoneflake, bow-drillkit, smallbarkvessel and tiny nutportion with existing pouch, no backpack or extra duplicatekit. Labels ‘KEEP AN EXIT’, ‘TEST THE CARRY’, ‘UNSUPPLIED SITE’. No fortifiedrefuge, cache, defensive trap, guaranteeorattack.

Scavenging
Skills page
Main isolated worn old RED-DEER SHED ANTLER fragment examined by one hand above dry grass, blunt cut base and branched tines recognisable, no skull attached. Secondary faint ground-sign inset has carnivoreprint and withdrawal arrow. Labels ‘DETACHED MATERIAL’, ‘CHECK CONDITION’, ‘LEAVE FRESH PREDATOR SIGN’. No active kill, meat pile, predator confrontation or stolen hominid equipment.

Shelter Construction
Skills page
Checking a light fork-and-rail bearing from outside before adding cover.

Simple Coiling and Weaving
Skills page
Two separate side-by-side basketry construction studies, clearly distinguish mechanisms. LEFT small spiral soft grass foundation with individual stitches linking new outer coil to preceding one; bone awl in a gap not puncturing thick wood. RIGHT upright slender willow stakes with ONE flexible working strand passing alternately in front/behind, open unfinished wall. Labels ‘COILED FOUNDATION’, ‘JOIN EACH COIL’, ‘STAKE AND STRAND’. No net or twining.

Simple Cordage
Skills page
Macro close study of two fibre bundles in hands being reverse wrapped into two-ply line. Each bundle’s own twist direction opposes the direction they wrap around each other. Use curved arrows one kind around bundle and opposite larger arrow around pair, physically traceable continuous fibres. Completed short line hangs below pinch point. Secondary inset shows staggered overlapping fibre joins at DIFFERENT positions in two strands. Labels ‘TWIST EACH BUNDLE’, ‘WRAP OPPOSITE’, ‘STAGGER JOINS’. No spindle or loom.

Simple Hafting
Skills page
A supported stone-and-wood joint with mechanical binding clear of the working edge.

Small Game Butchery
Skills page
Separated work zones: at left a clean slate with small neutral-coloured meat portions and a stone flake, at right one small fur pelt laid flat and a separate dirty scrap bowl. Cropped hands carefully draw a blunt scraper across the pelt’s cream underside, no exposed viscera, blood or carcass wound. Labels ‘CLEAN FOOD’, ‘PELT WORK’, ‘CLEAN IMPLEMENTS’. Illustrate contamination control and limited yield, not a slaughter scene.

Spear Throwing
Skills page
Two separate side-profile motion studies of the same robust upright human wearing modest simple skin clothing: balanced start and coordinated hand release. Correct human anatomy no overlapping ghost arms. LONG stone-pointed spear with knapped head bound into wooden shaft, cast BY HAND, no atlatl, bow or dart fletching. One tiny separate grouping diagram not numericalrange. Labels ‘COORDINATE THE BODY’, ‘CONTROL RELEASE’, ‘RETRIEVE AND INSPECT’. Generic explanatory skill, not protagonist competence or species-strength scale.

Stitching
Skills page
Close main study of two small overlapping pale rawhide scraps with widely spaced pre-pierced holes away from edges. A short bone eyed needle pulling one thin natural thread through both layers; a few completed even stitches beside it, needle fully separate from finger. Small detail shows hole too close to edge with tear compared to sound margin. Labels ‘PRE-PIERCE’, ‘EVEN TENSION’, ‘SOUND MARGIN’. No industrial thread, steel needle or modern fabric.

Stone Selection
Skills page
Two contrasted isolated stone samples: rounded tough percussor cobble and fine-grained core with one small clean conchoidal flake scar and separate sharpflake. Third small visibly crackedweathered rejectedcobble. A hand turns sound sample, not striking. Labels ‘PERCUSSOR’, ‘TEST FRACTURE’, ‘REJECT CRACKS’. No claimedhighgradeflint fromcolouralone, polishedgem, metaltool or hugecollection.

Tracking
Skills page
Three successive hoof-print pairs in soft soil, direction arrows along trackway, one weather-softened edge shown enlarged beside fresh-looking edge without claiming exact age. Small hands use plain uncalibrated reference stick for comparison. Labels ‘PATTERN’, ‘SUBSTRATE’, ‘CORROBORATE’. No certain species diagnosis from singleprint, timestamps, metricruler or guaranteedtrapcatch.

Tripod Lashing
Skills page
Three parallel wooden poles bound by several wraps around all three near aligned tops; close enlarged inset shows TWO frapping paths running in spaces between poles tightening wraps, not random wound cord. A small lower-right secondary study of same three poles spread into three-legged tripod with load arrow falling INSIDE triangular footprint. Exactly THREE poles and feet, no fourth. Labels ‘WRAPS’, ‘FRAPPING TURNS’, ‘LOAD INSIDE BASE’. Natural fibre cord no metal fasteners.

Twining
Skills page
Large macro technical study of FOUR upright pale willow strip foundations and EXACTLY TWO continuous working cords, one dusty blue and one muted coral for teaching distinction. The two cords CROSS in each space BETWEEN neighbouring foundations and change front/back position, enclosing each foundation, not an ordinary single-strand over/under weave. One completed row only, enlarged gap detail. Labels ‘TWO WORKING ELEMENTS’, ‘CROSS BETWEEN’, ‘FOUNDATIONS’. No loom, knots at every crossing or finished blanket.

index.title: Humanity Handbook
index.content:
A traveller arrives in northern Iberia around 40,000 years ago, carrying humanity’s knowledge in memory and nothing else. The handbook follows the work of turning that knowledge into practical capabilities, from the first shelter and fire to a society capable of planetary defence.
Start with The Mission and the Handbook, then the setting and the valley map.
Read the story
Begin the story →
The story follows one person’s trials, failures and discoveries. The reference pages describe the materials, skills, equipment and systems behind them.
Explore the handbook

The story — Follow the traveller from arrival, day by day.
Reflections — Read the arrival appraisal and milestone reviews.
Materials — Explore natural and manufactured stocks.
Skills — Find the practical abilities needed to make progress.
Tools and equipment — Browse objects, clothing, containers and machinery.
Structures and places — Explore construction and the places in the story.
Processes and systems — Connect resources, skills and equipment into working systems.
Historical eras — Use history as orientation for the route ahead.
Reference — Find the ledgers, dependencies and research notes.
The mission — Follow cooperation and the longer route to planetary defence.

Connect the pieces
Topic Index · Capability Dependency Map · Civilisation Roadmap · Survival Ledger
